title: Vegetarian Mapo Tofu
subtitle: Silken tofu in a numbing Sichuan sauce with mushrooms in place of pork
excerpt: All the ma la heat of the original -- doubanjiang, Sichuan peppercorns, chilli oil -- with finely chopped shiitake mushrooms swapped in for pork mince. The silken tofu barely needs cooking; the sauce does the work. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Mapo tofu (ma po dou fu) originates in Chengdu, Sichuan province, and is attributed to a pockmarked (ma) woman (po) who ran a restaurant near a bridge in the 1860s. The dish is documented in Lin Hsiang Ju and Lin Tsuifeng's Chinese Gastronomy (1969) and in detail in Fuchsia Dunlop's Sichuan Cookery (2001). The vegetarian adaptation, replacing pork with mushrooms, is a natural extension given the dish's Buddhist-friendly flavour profile and appears widely in contemporary Chinese vegetarian cooking.

content.text: This serves 4 with steamed rice and takes about 30 minutes. The characteristic
ma la
sensation -- numbness from Sichuan peppercorns, heat from chilli -- comes entirely from the sauce; the
silken tofu
simply absorbs it. Finely chopped shiitake mushrooms in place of pork mince provide enough texture and umami to make the swap seamless.

Handle the silken tofu carefully -- it tears easily. Cut it into 2 cm cubes and lower them gently into warm water for a few minutes before adding to the wok; this brings the tofu up to temperature so it does not cool the sauce. Add the cornflour slurry gradually, in stages, since the right consistency varies depending on how much liquid the tofu releases.

content.text: Method
Place the tofu cubes in a bowl of warm, lightly salted water and leave while you prepare the sauce. This firms the exterior slightly and brings the tofu to temperature so it does not chill the sauce.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the
doubanjiang
and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until the oil turns red and the paste smells toasted and fragrant.
Add the garlic, ginger, and fermented black beans. Cook for 1 minute, then add the chopped shiitake mushrooms. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until the mushrooms have wilted and are beginning to colour.

Pour in the vegetable stock and light soy sauce. Bring to a simmer, then drain the tofu cubes and lower them gently into the wok. Spoon the sauce over the top rather than stirring, to keep the cubes intact.

Simmer gently for 3 minutes. Then stir the cornflour slurry and pour half of it into the wok, gently shaking the pan to incorporate. Add the rest if the sauce is still thin. It should be thick enough to coat the tofu and flow slowly when the wok is tilted.
Add the chilli oil and half the ground
Sichuan peppercorns
. Gently fold through. Transfer to a serving bowl, scatter over the remaining ground peppercorns and the spring onions. Serve with rice.

items.symptom: Tofu is broken into small pieces
items.cause: Stirred too vigorously, or the tofu was added to a very high heat
items.fix: Use a soft spatula or spoon and tilt/shake the wok instead of stirring. Lower the heat to a gentle simmer before adding the tofu.

items.symptom: Sauce is watery and does not coat the tofu
items.cause: The tofu released water into the sauce as it cooked
items.fix: Add the remaining cornflour slurry in stages until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. A pre-soak in salted warm water reduces water release.

items.cause: Sichuan peppercorns were old or the finishing step was skipped
items.fix: Toast fresh Sichuan peppercorns until they pop and smell citrusy, then grind. Add half to the finished dish as a direct finish, not just during cooking.

content.text: Where this dish lives

Vegetarian mapo tofu is common in Chinese Buddhist cooking, where pork is replaced with mushrooms. The Sichuan flavour profile stays the same. This version is lighter than the meat original. Use vegetable stock and plant-based oyster sauce to make it fully vegan.
